summary: Steel fire tower, 30 m, built 2019 per Alberta's register; active, access mode drive, with a weather station. No history or visit information found.

access.note: Register lists access mode as drive and the tower as active. No source describes public visits today.

events.note: Register construction year for the steel tower now listed.

evidence.supports: Register: steel, built 2019, 30 m tower, 1,289 m elevation
Register coordinates place the tower in west-central Alberta
Register: location verified; active; access mode drive
OpenStreetMap lists the site as an observation tower

evidence.quote: 127 wildfire lookout sites are located throughout Alberta's boreal forest and along the Rocky Mountains.

evidence.supports: Province-wide: each site staffed by a lookout observer, generally April to October
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.

evidence.supports: Agency: Wildfire staff sit within Agriculture and Forestry
evidence.quote: Wildfire staff with Agriculture and Forestry have adopted a number of Alberta BearSmart recommendations

corrections.why: Register lists the tower as active with access mode drive. No source says it is closed to visitors, so restricted is the level the sources support.

sources.title: Wildfire Lookouts of Alberta (WF_WILDFIRE_LOOKOUT), FIRES database extract
Tom Hill Fire Lookout, OpenStreetMap node 5540677295

notes_for_editor: Only the register, one OpenStreetMap node and Alberta's province-wide lookout pages describe this tower. No history, name origin or visit information was found after two searches. The register's drive access is recorded as reachable by road; it does not establish that the public may visit. Access 'restricted' is an editorial level from working status, not a stated rule. Brief's access 'closed' is not supported as a site status.
